Phrase matches are safer than broad for budget control. The rerun post is the best keyword match. There is concern that narrow keywords might not spend the full $95.
Posts accepted. Now adding keywords.

English should be added to the remaining line items too. This prevents non-English speakers in the UK and Ireland from seeing the content. Welsh, Irish, and Polish are among the languages that need coverage.

The Black Friday campaign is live and serving.

I'll check campaign stats periodically over the 9-day period. The first optimization pass will wait until after the first full day to ensure enough data has populated.

I'll check campaign performance at five specific times: after the first day, mid-week, the morning of Black Friday, late on the 29th, and again at the end of the 30th. I'll use wait_until to pause between checks.

I'll check delivery status after six hours to catch any approval or serving delays early. The first optimization pass will wait until Sunday morning for a full day of data.

I'll pause the session until noon UK today. I'll check the stats schema for engagement and billing metrics when I resume.
Checking stats 12 hours later. Need metric groups.

The 12-hour results show a product offer.

The 12-hour results show only five link clicks total. The "cirm4" offer had the highest CTR at 0.064%. The "r3zhe" deadline post had the best CPC at $4.36 and the highest CTR at 0.33%. The "jxq3i" keyword post had the lowest CPC at $2.48 and the cheapest CPM at $1.36. These are early metrics and should not be overinterpreted.

Total spend is $21.82 across four posts, about half the daily budget of $57. The deadline post is burning through its $10 cap quickly and may need a budget increase. No major changes should be made until more data arrives.

The deadline post may hit its daily cap by noon and stop. The keyword post is underspending, likely due to a narrow audience. I will wait until Sunday evening or Monday morning before making any changes, since B2B audiences are more active on weekdays.

B2B traffic is weaker on weekends. The real signal comes Monday and Tuesday when engineers are at work. Saturday data should not be used to kill weekend creatives. The deadline post may need its daily budget lowered if it burns through its cap quickly, but that is too early to decide. I will check Sunday evening briefly for delivery issues, then optimize Monday morning.
Gathering statistics from the start of the week through Sunday at 6pm UK.

The keyword ad targets in-market queries like "flaky tests" and "GitHub Actions," so clicks are likely higher quality even without the offer copy in the tweet. The £0 post carries the offer but uses weak CTR and interest targeting, which reaches a broader, less relevant audience. This explains why keyword clicks convert cheaper than interest-targeted ones.

The remaining budget of roughly $424 should be spread across the seven days left, which means about $60 per day. The current daily caps total $57, so the full $500 budget is on track to be spent.

The product campaign’s billing discrepancy likely stems from AUTO bid optimization events. X may charge for engagement events rather than only link clicks, which would explain the 85 billed engagements against just 6 actual link clicks.

The £0 campaign will not be paused immediately. It still carries the offer creative in market, and it will only be shut down if it remains unprofitable through Monday.

I cannot delete promoted tweets, so adding a second creative to the winning keyword line item is risky. If the new post underperforms, it could steal budget from the better-performing one. I am searching again for a delete tool.

I will not create a competing line item. The winning keyword campaign will receive the extra budget, and the losing line will be cut. I cannot edit the existing post, so I will add high-intent keywords like "flaky," "gitlab pipeline," and "ci cd" to the winner to ensure the extra spend finds inventory.

If delivery cannot scale, CPC will rise and that will be visible by Monday.
